tools.name: search
tools.description:
Use when the user asks to find or look up a monday.com board, item, doc, dashboard, folder, workspace, update, or timeline item by name or keyword. Search within monday.com platform. Supported searchType values: BOARD, DOCUMENTS, FOLDERS, WORKSPACES, UPDATES, ITEMS, TIMELINE_ITEMS, DASHBOARDS.
searchTerm is the phrase the search matches against — the text/keywords to look for (e.g. a board name, i

searchTerm.description: The search phrase — the text the search matches results against (e.g. a board name, item title, or keywords). Required and must be non-empty. This is NOT a filter or an id — pass the words to look for. searchTerm is required and must be a non-empty search string. To browse or list without a search term, use workspace_info (for boards, docs, and folders in a workspace) or get_board_items_page (for items within a specific board).

searchType.description: The type of search to perform. Valid values: BOARD, DOCUMENTS, FOLDERS, WORKSPACES, UPDATES, ITEMS, TIMELINE_ITEMS, DASHBOARDS.

limit.description: The number of items to get. Maximum is 20.

strategy.description: Search strategy, trading result quality against latency. SPEED: keyword matching only — no semantic retrieval, no reranking; fastest. BALANCED (used when omitted): keyword and semantic retrieval fused together. QUALITY: BALANCED plus AI reranking of the results; slowest. Start with SPEED and escalate to BALANCED, then QUALITY, only when it returns no or clearly irrelevant results. Every strategy — SPEED most of all — favors short, keyword-based search terms: most terms must match, so extra words cut results. Prefer several focused searches over one long one. Applies to BOARD, ITEMS, DOCUMENTS, UPDATES, DASHBOARDS search; ignored for other searchTypes.

workspaceIds.description: Array of workspace IDs (numbers) to search in. Optional for FOLDERS search (searches all accessible workspaces when omitted). For ITEMS, BOARD, DOCUMENTS, DASHBOARDS, UPDATES, and TIMELINE_ITEMS search, only pass this if the user explicitly asked to search within specific workspaces. Example: [12345, 67890].

boardIds.description: Array of board IDs (numbers) to scope the search to. Applies to BOARD, ITEMS, UPDATES, and TIMELINE_ITEMS search. Only pass it if the user explicitly asked to search within specific boards. Example: [12345, 67890].

creatorIds.description: Array of user IDs (numbers) to filter by creator. Applies to ITEMS (filters by item creator), UPDATES (filters by update author), and DASHBOARDS (filters by dashboard creator). Only pass it if the user explicitly asked to filter by specific creators. Example: [12345, 67890].

personIds.description: Filter (ITEMS only): user IDs (numbers). Matches items with any of these users assigned in any of their people columns — every person and team column of the item is checked, not one specific column. At most 50 unique IDs in total across personIds and teamIds. Values are alternatives (any of); all provided filters must be satisfied (AND). Only pass it if the user explicitly asked to filter by assigned people. Example: [12345, 67890].

teamIds.description: Filter (ITEMS only): team IDs (numbers). Matches items with any of these teams assigned in any of their people columns — every person and team column of the item is checked, not one specific column. At most 50 unique IDs in total across personIds and teamIds. Values are alternatives (any of); all provided filters must be satisfied (AND). Only pass it if the user explicitly asked to filter by assigned teams. Example: [12345].

statusLabels.description: Filter (ITEMS only): status labels (e.g. "Done", "Stuck"). Matches items where any of their status columns has one of these labels — every status-type column of the item is checked, not one specific column, including columns titled e.g. "Label" or "Priority", which are status columns too. Whole-label match, ignoring case. At most 10 labels. Values are alternatives (any of); all provided filters must be satisfied (AND). Only pass it if the user explicitly asked to filter by status. Example: ["Done", "Stuck"].

tagNames.description: Filter (ITEMS only): tag names (e.g. "bug", "q3-launch"). Matches items tagged with any of these tags — every tags column of the item is checked, not one specific column. Whole-name match, ignoring case; a leading "#" is ignored. At most 10 tags. Values are alternatives (any of); all provided filters must be satisfied (AND). Only pass it if the user explicitly asked to filter by tags. Example: ["bug", "urgent"].

docIds.description: Array of document IDs (numbers), as they appear in document URLs, to scope the search to. Applies to DOCUMENTS search, with at most 512 ids. Use it to search within a known set of documents, for example to find which of them mention a term. Only pass it if the user explicitly asked to search within specific documents. Example: [12345, 67890].

itemIds.description: Array of item IDs (numbers) to scope TIMELINE_ITEMS search to the timeline of specific items. Only applies to TIMELINE_ITEMS search. Example: [12345, 67890].

timelineItemType.description: Filter TIMELINE_ITEMS search by timeline item type, e.g. "email", "note", "meeting", "phoneCall". Only applies to TIMELINE_ITEMS search.

timelineProductKind.description: Filter TIMELINE_ITEMS search by the product the timeline item originates from. Only applies to TIMELINE_ITEMS search.

overviewKinds.description: Filter DASHBOARDS search by dashboard visibility. Only applies to DASHBOARDS search. Example: ["public"].

dateRange.description: Filter results by creation and/or last-update date. Applies to every searchType except FOLDERS. Each bound is optional and must be a UTC datetime in the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ, e.g. { "created_after": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" }. Only pass it if the user asked for a time window.

created_after.description: Only results created at or after this date. UTC datetime in the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ, e.g. 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z.

created_before.description: Only results created at or before this date. UTC datetime in the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ, e.g. 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z.

updated_after.description: Only results last updated at or after this date. UTC datetime in the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ, e.g. 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z.

updated_before.description: Only results last updated at or before this date. UTC datetime in the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ, e.g. 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z.

tools.name: get_board_info
tools.description: Get comprehensive board information including metadata, structure, owners, and configuration. Set includeKnowledge to true when you need to interpret the board rather than just read its configuration: for example, choosing a status, label or column value from the user's intent instead of an exact name they gave, or explaining what statuses, columns or roles mean. Not needed for structural work suc

boardId.description: The id of the board to get information for

includeKnowledge.description: Optional. Returns generated business context: workflow and status meanings, column purposes, people roles, related boards. Set it when you must interpret the board, e.g. pick a status from the user's intent rather than an exact label name. Leave it off for structural lookups. Adds latency and may be null while being generated. Defaults to false.

includeSubscribers.description: Optional. Set to true to also return the board subscribers and team subscribers (id and name). Subscribers include both people and AI agents subscribed to the board (agents appear with their agent user id). Omitted by default because the subscriber list can be long on large boards. Defaults to false.

ids.description: Optional. Restrict returned views to these view ids.

names.description: Optional. Restrict returned views to these view names (case-insensitive). The tool resolves names via a lean id/name index query first to avoid downloading every view on large boards.

only.description: Optional. When true, omit columns and return only views plus the board metadata needed around them.

ids.description: Optional. Restrict returned columns to these column ids.

only.description: Optional. When true, omit views and return only columns plus the board metadata needed around them.

filters.description: Optional response-shaping filters for large boards. Omit to return the full board info payload.

tools.name: get_board_items_page
tools.description:
Get items from a monday.com board: list, filter, sort, search and paginate board items with their column values, groups, subitems and item descriptions.
Returns structured JSON with board info (id, name, hierarchy_type), item details (id, name, url, created_at, updated_at, parent_item_id) and pagination (has_more, nextCursor, count). Use nextCursor from the response as cursor to get the next page

boardId.description: The id of the board to get items from. Required, including when paging with cursor.

itemIds.description: The ids of the items to get. The count of items should be less than 100.

searchTerm.description: The search term to use for the search. Use this when the user provides a vague, incomplete, or approximate search term (e.g. "marketing campaign", "John's task", "budget-related") and there is no clear exact compare value for a specific column. Do not use this when the user specifies an exact value that maps directly to a column comparison (e.g. name contains "marketing campaign", status = "Done", priority = "High", owner = "Daniel") - prefer structured filters in those cases.

limit.description: The number of items to get, up to 2000. Requests above 500 are served only by the items_page implementation; the few requests that fall back to the monday API return 500 items with a warning and a cursor for the rest.

cursor.description: The cursor to get the next page of items, use the nextCursor from the previous response. If nextCursor was null there is no next page to fetch (has_more says whether the result is complete). Filters, orderBy, itemIds and searchTerm are encoded in the cursor and ignored when a cursor is provided.

includeColumns.description: Whether to include column values in the response. PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION: only set this to true when you actually need the column data. Excluding columns significantly reduces token usage and improves response latency. If you only need to count items, get item ids/names, or check if items exist, keep this false.

includeGroup.description: Whether to include each item's board group (id and title) in the response. Set to false to reduce token usage when group membership is not needed.

includeItemDescription.description: Whether to include the item's description in the response. The item description is the rich-text body content inside a monday.com item (similar to a task description or issue body). Set this to true when the user asks about an item's description, details, body, or notes. PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION: only set this to true when you actually need the description content.

includeSubItems.description: Whether to include sub items in the response. PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION: only set this to true when you actually need the sub items data.

includeIsLeaf.description: Multi-level boards: whether to return is_leaf on each item (true when it has no subitems). It is already returned with includeColumns, includeSubItems or hierarchyScope; set this to get it without them. PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION: only set this to true when you need it, since it reads the board with relations.

subItemLimit.description: The number of sub items to get per item. Only used when includeSubItems is true.

hierarchyScope.description: Multi-level boards only. "allItems": filters match items at every level and each match is returned as its own item. With includeColumns and no columnIds, parent_item_id may be missing when the parent is not in the same response (for example, it did not match the filter). "parentItems" (monday default): matches are returned as their top-level item. Ignored on classic boards. Encoded in the cursor and ignored when a cursor is provided.

filters.description: The configuration of filters to apply on the items. Use get_board_info with filters.columns.only for the column ids and types on the board. Before sending filters, call get_column_type_info with fetchMode "guidelines" for each column type and follow data.guidelines.filter (null if that type has no documented rules). Invalid rules are rejected with a structured error that names the offending rule.

columnId.description: Ordinary column ids are board-specific. Use get_board_info with filters.columns.only to get them for the current board. Also accepts four virtual columns that get_board_info does not return: "group" (the group id goes in compareValue, e.g. "group_mm6wsvcc" - the columnId itself is always the literal "group"), "__creation_log__", "__last_updated__" and "__item_id__".

compareValue.description: The value to compare the attribute to. A string, number, boolean or an array of them, depending on the column type: status, dropdown, numbers and checkbox columns compare against their numeric index/value (e.g. 1, not "Done"); text and date columns compare against strings. The operators within_the_last and within_the_next are the exception: they take a two item array of [UNIT, AMOUNT] such as ["DAYS", 7]. Optional only for is_empty / is_not_empty.

compareAttribute.description: The attribute to compare the value to (e.g. "text"). Optional.

operator.description: The operator to use for the filter

filtersOperator.description: The operator to use to combine the filters

columnIds.description: The ids of the item columns and subitem columns to get. Use it to reduce the response size when the user asks for specific columns. Only used when includeColumns is true. If not provided, all columns are returned.

orderBy.description: The columns to order by; controls the order of the items in the response.

columnId.description: Ordinary column ids are board-specific. Use get_board_info with filters.columns.only to get them for the current board. Also accepts four virtual columns that get_board_info does not return: "group", "__creation_log__", "__last_updated__" and "__item_id__".

tools.name: get_column_type_info
tools.description: Retrieves comprehensive information about a specific column type. Use fetchMode "schema" (default) to get the JSON schema definition from the API — to understand structure, validation rules, and available properties for column settings. Call this BEFORE any tool that writes column settings: create_column, update_column, and manage_object_schema_columns. Use fetchMode "guidelines" to get only guide

columnType.description: The column type to retrieve information for (e.g., "text", "status", "date", "numbers")

fetchMode.description: fetchMode "schema": JSON settings schema only (GraphQL). fetchMode "guidelines": guidelines.filter and guidelines.aggregation only — no GraphQL round-trip.

tools.name: get_board_activity
tools.description: Get board activity logs for a specified time range (defaults to last 30 days, up to the last 90 days). Optionally filter by item ids or user ids to avoid fetching activity for the entire board. [REQUIRED PRECONDITION]: Call this with includeData=true before undo_action — it is the source of the action_record_uuid that identifies the action to undo.

boardId.description: The id of the board to get activity for

itemIds.description: Filter activity to specific item ids. Omit to get activity for the whole board.

userIds.description: Filter activity to actions performed by specific user ids.

fromDate.description: Start date for activity range (ISO8601DateTime format). Defaults to 30 days ago. Limited to the last 90 days. Older dates are clamped to 90 days ago

toDate.description: End date for activity range (ISO8601DateTime format). Defaults to now

includeData.description: Whether to include the raw data payload for each activity entry. The data field contains the full before/after state of changes and can be very large. Only set to true when you need the detailed change data.

tools.name: get_activity_logs
tools.description: Use when the user asks what changed, who did something, or what happened on monday.com boards, items or users over a period of time. Reads the monday.com activity log: who changed what, and when. Requires at least one of board_ids, user_ids or correlation_ids. Narrow the query with item_ids, event_types, entities, search and a time range (last_hours, or from/to; at most the last 90 days) rather th

board_ids.description: Board IDs to read activity from. Only boards the user can see return events.

user_ids.description: IDs of the users who performed the actions. Pass the current user's ID for "what did I do".

correlation_ids.description: Correlation IDs grouping the events of one logical session, e.g. one agent conversation.

item_ids.description: Narrow to events on these items. Combine with board_ids.

event_types.description: Narrow to these event types, e.g. "create_pulse", "delete_pulse", "update_column_value".

entities.description: Narrow to these entity types, e.g. "pulse" (item), "board", "update".

search.description: Free-text prefix search over item names.

last_hours.description: Only events from the last N hours (max 2136). Use instead of "from" when you do not know the current time.

from.description: ISO 8601 start of the time range, inclusive. At most 90 days ago. Not with last_hours.

to.description: ISO 8601 end of the time range. Defaults to now.

limit.description: Maximum events to return, newest first (default 25, max 200).

cursor.description: The cursor from a previous response, to fetch the next page with the same filters. It keeps the time window of the first page.

include_data.description: Include each event's data payload (column values, names, before/after). Off by default. Payloads share a 256 KB budget per call; events past it come back with data_truncated: true — re-query those with narrower filters or a smaller limit.

      3. Use 'getMe: true' to get current user information
      4. AVOID broad queries (no parameters) - use only as last resort

      REQUIRED PARAMETER PRIORITY (use in this order):
      1. getM

userIds.description: Specific user IDs to fetch.[IMPORTANT] ALWAYS use when you have user IDs in context. PREFER over general search. RETURNS: user profiles including team memberships

teamIds.description:
Specific team IDs to fetch.[IMPORTANT] ALWAYS use when you have team IDs in context, NEVER fetch all teams if specific IDs are available.

teamsOnly.description: Fetch only teams, no users returned. Combine with includeTeamMembers for member details.

includeTeamMembers.description: Set to true only when you need additional member details for teams other than names and ids.

tools.name: workspace_info
tools.description: This tool returns the boards, docs and folders in a workspace and which folder they are in. It returns up to 100 of each object type, if you receive 100 assume there are additional objects of that type in the workspace.

workspace_id.description: The ID of the workspace to get information for

tools.name: list_workspaces

List all workspaces available to the user, ordered by membership (user's workspaces first). Returns workspaces with their ID, name, and description.
[IMPORTANT] To search for workspaces by name, use the "search" tool with searchType WORKSPACES instead — it provides faster and more accurate results.

limit.description: Number of workspaces to return. Default is (100), lower for a smaller response size

tools.name: read_docs
tools.description:
Get information about monday.com documents. Supports two modes:

MODE: "content" (default) — Fetch documents with their full markdown content.
- Requires: type ("ids" | "object_ids" | "workspace_ids") and ids array
- For a doc that lives as a board view, pass board_id and view_id instead of type/ids. They are the ids in the board URL: https://<slug>.monday.com/boards/<board_id>/views/<view_id>. Om

mode.description: The operation mode. "content" (default) fetches documents with their markdown content. "version_history" fetches the edit history of a single document.

type.description: Query type for content mode: "ids", "object_ids", or "workspace_ids". Required when mode is "content", unless board_id is provided. Default to "object_ids" — the number in a doc URL is an object_id. Use "ids" only for the internal doc id field returned by read_docs, and "workspace_ids" only to list all docs in a workspace.

board_id.description: For docs that live as a board view: the <board_id> in https://<slug>.monday.com/boards/<board_id>/views/<view_id>. Use this instead of type/ids when all you have is a board view URL. Only used in content mode.

view_id.description: For a doc that lives as a board view: the <view_id> in https://<slug>.monday.com/boards/<board_id>/views/<view_id>. Requires board_id. Omit to read every doc view of the board.

ids.description: Array of ID values. In content mode: matches the query type (ids/object_ids/workspace_ids). In version_history mode: provide the single document object_id here (e.g., ids: ["5001466606"]).

limit.description: Number of docs per page (default: 25). Only used in content mode.

order_by.description: Order in which to retrieve docs. Only used in content mode.

page.description: Page number to return (starts at 1). Only used in content mode.

include_blocks.description: If true, includes the blocks array (block IDs, types, positions, content) in the response. Required when you plan to call update_doc. Defaults to false to reduce response size. Only used in content mode.

blocks_limit.description: Maximum number of blocks to return per document (default: 25). Only used in content mode when include_blocks is true.

blocks_page.description: Page number for block pagination, starting at 1. Omit to use the API default. Use with blocks_limit to page through documents with more than 25 blocks. Only used in content mode when include_blocks is true.

include_comments.description: If true, fetches all comments and replies on the document. Comments are stored at the item level within the doc backing board. Defaults to false. Only used in content mode.

comments_limit.description: Maximum number of comments (updates) to fetch per item when include_comments is true. Defaults to 50. Only used in content mode.

version_history_limit.description: Maximum number of restoring points to return. Use this when the user asks for "last N changes". Only used in version_history mode.

since.description: ISO 8601 date string to filter version history from (e.g., "2026-03-15T00:00:00Z"). If omitted, returns the full history. Only used in version_history mode.

until.description: ISO 8601 date string to filter version history until (e.g., "2026-03-16T23:59:59Z"). Defaults to now. Only used in version_history mode.

include_diff.description: If true, fetches content diffs between consecutive restoring points. May be slower due to additional API calls. Only used in version_history mode.

tools.name: submit_bug_or_feature_request
tools.description:
Report a bug, submit a feature request, or share feedback about the monday.com product or this integration.

Call this tool proactively — not just when a user explicitly asks. Use it whenever any of these signals show up:
• A tool produced unexpected errors, empty results, or needed a workaround
• The user tried something monday.com couldn't support and had to settle for a partial or manual soluti

kind.description: The kind of submission: general feedback, a feature request, or a bug report

title.description: A short summary of the feedback. Do NOT include any personally identifiable information (PII) such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, or any other personal data.

description.description: Full details — what happened, what was expected, or what is being requested. Do NOT include any personally identifiable information (PII) such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, or any other personal data.

tool_name.description: The name of the monday.com MCP tool this feedback is about, if applicable (e.g. "create_item", "get_board_info"). Only include monday.com MCP tool names — do not reference tools from other connected services.

tools.name: create_item
tools.description: Create a single item or subitem on a monday.com board, or duplicate an existing item. [IMPORTANT] If you need to create multiple items in one call, use create_items instead of calling this tool in a loop. Otherwise: create a new item with provided values, create a subitem under a parent item, or duplicate an existing item and update it with new values. Use parentItemId when creating a subitem unde

boardId.description: The id of the board to which the new item will be added

name.description: The name of the new item to be created, must be relevant to the user's request. 1–255 characters.

groupId.description: The id of the group id to which the new item will be added, if its not clearly specified, leave empty. Not supported when duplicateFromItemId is a subitem.

columnValues.description: Pass a JSON object serialized once as a string, keyed by column id — not a JSON string of a JSON string. Column ids and labels must come from get_board_info for this board, people ids from list_users_and_teams, never guessed. Formats by column type: text and numbers: "value". long_text: {"text": "..."}. status: {"label": "Done"} or {"index": 1}, and the label must already exist unless createLabelsIfMissing is true. dropdown: {"labels": ["A"]} or {"ids": [1]} — always an array, even for one value. date: {"date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}. timeline: {"from": "YYYY-MM-DD", "to": "YYYY-MM-DD"}. people: {"personsAndTeams": [{"id": 123, "kind": "person"}]}, where kind is "person", "team" or "agent". Plain strings fail for email and phone. null clears a column. Example: {"text_col": "New text", "status_col": {"label": "Done"}, "dropdown_col": {"labels": ["A"]}, "date_col": {"date": "2023-05-25"}}

createLabelsIfMissing.description: When true, missing status/dropdown labels referenced in columnValues will be auto-created on the board instead of erroring with ColumnValueException. Requires permission to change board structure. Use when the caller specifies label names that may not yet exist on the board.

duplicateFromItemId.description: The id of existing item to duplicate and update with new values (only provide when duplicating)

operations.description:
Ordered list of operations to perform. Executed sequentially. Stops at first failure.

Operation types:
- set_name: Rename the document.
- add_markdown_content: Append markdown as blocks (simplest for text/lists/tables).
- update_block: Change content of an existing text/code/list/divider block.
- create_block: Create a new block at a specific position (supports text, list_item, code, divider, page_break, image, video, notice_box, table, layout).
- delete_blocks: Permanently delete 1–100 blocks in one call. Provide all block IDs in the block_ids array. Works for all block types including BOARD, WIDGET, DOC embed, and GIPHY.
- replace_block: Delete a block and create a new one in its place. Use for: changing image/video source, table restructure, notice_box theme change.
- add_comment: Create a new comment or reply on the document. Use parent_update_id to reply to an existing comment. Format text with HTML. Uses the doc's backing board item.

WHEN TO USE WHICH:
- Adding new text sections → add_markdown_content
- Adding asset-based images → create_block with block_type "image" and asset_id (add_markdown_content does NOT support asset images)
- Mixed content with asset images → alternate add_markdown_content (for text) and create_block (for each image) in sequence
- Editing existing text block → update_block
- Changing an image URL → replace_block (image URL is immutable after creation)
- Changing video URL → replace_block
- Restructuring a table → replace_block
- BOARD/WIDGET/DOC/GIPHY blocks → delete_blocks only (no public API to create these)

NESTING CONTENT IN CONTAINERS:
- notice_box: Fully supported. Create the notice_box first, then in a separate call create child blocks with parent_block_id set to the notice_box ID. You cannot reference a block ID created in the same call.
- table: Cell-level API nesting is NOT supported. To create a table with content, use add_markdown_content with a markdown table (e.g. "| H1 | H2 |\n| --- | --- |\n| A | B |"). This creates a pre-populated table in one shot. Empty tables created via create_block cannot have their cells populated through the API.
- layout: Cell-level API nesting is NOT supported and there is no markdown equivalent. Layouts can only be created empty via create_block. No workaround exists to populate layout columns through the API.
Deleting a container does NOT delete its children — delete children first for clean removal.

BATCHING: delete_blocks accepts 1..100 IDs. Put ALL IDs in one operation's block_ids array. Never emit multiple delete_blocks operations in a row.

Block IDs are available in the blocks array returned by read_docs.

Ask a question about monday.com and get an AI-generated answer from the official knowledge base.

Use kind="general" for questions about using monday.com — features, automations, UI, help center, and settings. Returns cited source articles with links.
Use kind="developer_docs" for questions about the monday.com API — GraphQL queries and mutations, authentication, rate limits, webhooks, schema, API

kind.description: The knowledge domain to search. Use "developer_docs" for questions about the monday.com API — GraphQL queries and mutations, authentication, rate limits, webhooks, schema, API best practices, and building apps. Use "general" for questions about using monday.com — features, automations, UI, help center, and settings.

tools.name: manage_agent_jobs
tools.description:
Manage jobs on a monday platform agent.
Jobs define WHAT work runs and own one or more triggers that define WHEN it runs.

ACTIONS:
- list:   { action:"list", agent_id } — returns jobs, their instructions, stable ids, and nested triggers.
- create: { action:"create", agent_id, name?, instructions?, enabled?, triggers?, model?, thinking_level? }
- update: { action:"update", agent_id, job_id, name?,

action.description: "list" — inspect jobs and nested triggers. "create" — create a job. "update" — patch a job and its triggers. "delete" — remove a job and all nested triggers. "run" — run a job once now.

job_id.description: Required for update/delete/run. Stable job UUID returned by list/create.

name.description: Used with create/update. Display name of the job.

instructions.description: Used with create/update. Job-specific instructions followed whenever this job runs.

enabled.description: Used with create/update. Whether this job is enabled.

triggers.description: Triggers to create or update. Omitted existing triggers remain unchanged.

field_values.description: Trigger configuration matching field_schemas from agent_catalog.

remove_trigger_ids.description: Used with update. Stable trigger UUIDs to remove from this job.

model.description: Used with create/update. Omit unless the user asks for a model for this job: the job then runs on the agent's model. A catalog model id pins one, "auto" lets the platform choose, and "agent_default" removes the job's own model on update.

thinking_level.description: Used with create/update. Thinking level for the job's own model. The job never inherits the agent's level: omit it and the job's model runs at that model's own default. Without model, changes the level of the job's existing model; a job that follows the agent has none, so pass model too.

tools.name: get_workflow_editor_link
tools.description:
Creates the link that opens a workflow in the monday workflow editor, and saves a short summary of this conversation that the editor's chat shows the user, so they can continue there.

When to call: when the user asks for the workflow's link, or when you are done creating or changing a workflow, including a new empty one. Call it after every other change to the workflow has returned.

After callin

workflowObjectId.description: The identifier of a workflow object, found in the workflow URL or returned by create_workflow. A workflow object is the entity that is retained across published versions; users can create draft versions related to this workflow object. This is NOT an automation id: the workflowId returned by create_automation identifies a board automation, which these tools cannot address.

askedFor.description: What the user asked for, in their terms.

built.description: What the whole workflow does now, not only what changed last. Say so if it has no steps yet.

notDone.description: What the user asked for that is not built yet. Empty if nothing.

nextSteps.description: What the user should do next in the editor, such as connecting an account or publishing. Empty if nothing.

summary.description: A short handoff of this conversation.
